text:
sasha: quick sync: we need final agreement on the trace header contract (what lives in X-Redwood-Trace vs payload) and how billing_key is propagated. this is blocking schema slimdown PRs and the cardinality budget work.
frank: tl;dr: prefer minimal headers. put only trace_id + parent_id + sampled flag in header, everything else in the out-of-band envelope. headers traverse proxies easily and are cheap.
mai: i'm worried about cross-service cost attribution if billing_key isn't in the header. network-level hops sometimes drop payloads. ops wants an option to carry a small stable tenant_key in headers for edge cases.
anya: we saw dropped payload attributes in mobile SDK due to body size limits. a tiny header (billing_hint) would help, but it increases cardinality on our ingress routers. need caps.
lucas: proposal: two-tier header model: (1) required: X-RW-TID, X-RW-PID, X-RW-SAMP; (2) optional sticky: X-RW-TENANT-HINT (hashed) and X-RW-BILLING-HASH (32b). routers index only hashed hint and treat it as low-cardinality.
sasha: hashing is fine, but what about collisions impacting billing joins? we can't misattribute spend at scale. we should use a salted stable-hash per-tenant so collisions are negligible and revocable.
frank: salted hash + 64-bit farmhash should be safe. collisions <1e-12. we still need lookup path from billing-hash -> billing_key in the enrichment step. enrichment can expand it.
mai: that means early routing decisions can use hash only. downstream enrichment adds the canonical billing_key into envelopes. good.
anya: downside: some customer queries rely on human-readable tenant_ids in traces today. hashing will break that in ad-hoc debugging. we should keep a foldable debug header X-RW-TENANT-DEBUG but only allowed internal-to-infra and stripped at egress.
lucas: agree. enforce stripping via edge filter and log an alert if a non-infra token carries debug header.
sasha: question: where do we enforce cardinality caps? ingress? enrich? both?
frank: enforce at ingress with sampling + sink-to-metrics for over-cardinality. enrichment should reject expansion beyond a configured threshold and mark trace as partial with reason=card_limit.
anya: implement a fast path in ingest: if tenant-hash not in known-tenants cache, tag as unknown and route to limited-enrich queue to avoid spikes. known-tenants pass through full enrich.
mai: ops asks for a migration plan: we need dual-write period where both old header (billing_key) and new hashed header accepted, and enrich reads either. timeline?
lucas: propose dual-write for 4 weeks, with metrics: percent of traffic with new hash header, percent of enrich hits from cache, and collisions observed. after 4w, start rejecting old header except from trusted agents.
sasha: tests: please include fuzz tests for header parsing, and a synthetic load that generates 10k distinct tenant-hashes to validate router index performance.
frank: i'll add unit + load tests. also a small config: router index keeps top-1000 tenant-hashes per minute; beyond that we drop to aggregate buckets. prevents index explosion.
anya: impl note: enrich should accept billing-hash and return billing_key in envelope. add field billing_key_source: [header|enrichment|legacy] to trace envelope for audit.
mai: excellent — that field will help debugging unknown attributions.
deploy-bot: rollout plan frozen: canary ingest filter + header parsing (job: deploy-2026-03-20-headers). watch metric: router_index_evictions and enrich_cache_miss_rate.
lucas: runbook item: on router_index_evictions spike, toggle fallback mode to aggregate-billing and alert on suspected spammers. also contact infra-team to raise index size temporarily.
sasha: final asks before I write RFC addendum: exact header names, hash algorithm, dual-write window, and test matrix. can ppl ack ownership?
frank: owning router + hash impl. will PR with farmhash64 + salt rotation plan.
anya: owning ingest filter + limited-enrich queue work.
lucas: owning metrics + runbook entries. i'll create grafana panels and alerts.
mai: i'll coordinate dual-write rollout with partner teams and draft the RFC section on migration.
deploy-bot: canary deployed to staging cluster-3. monitor: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/headers
sasha: thanks all. I'll add the header contract snippet to the RFC follow-up and share a small compatibility checker script we can run against services. :sparkles:
